text: . India’s foreign exchange reserves rose by 14.1 billion US dollars (USD) to 707 billion US dollars during the week ended August 7. According to the Reserve Bank of India data, Foreign currency assets, the largest component of the reserves, increased by 9.9 billion USD to 574.6 billion USD during the week.Gold reserves added 3.9 billion USD to 108.7 billion US dollars. The country’s reserve position with the International Monetary Fund was up by 116 million USD to around 4.9 billion USD. Special Drawing Rights increased by 79 million USD to 18.74 billion USD.

. Wildfires continue to spread across parts of Europe as countries battle one of the hottest and driest summers on record. In Belgium, one of the country’s largest wildfires continued to burn in the eastern High Fens, near the German border, despite cooler weather and overnight rain. King Philippe visited emergency services battling the blaze. Dozens of firefighters, supported by aircraft from Norway, Sweden, Germany and the Netherlands, are working to contain the fire.In Greece, investigators are examining a wildfire on the island of Salamina that killed two people, injured nine and destroyed several homes. Another fire broke out near Spata, east of Athens, close to the capital’s international airport.Meanwhile, in southwestern France, a wildfire in the Landes region has been brought under control after four days of firefighting. Authorities have begun allowing some of the over 600 evacuated residents to return home as temperatures ease.A recent study has linked Europe’s extreme heat and dry conditions to climate change.

. In Men’s Cricket, Indian bowlers restricted Hosts Sri Lanka at 284 in their first innings, taking a lead of 178 runs at Stumps on Day 3 of the first Test in Galle. Manav Suthar led the wickets column for India with four scalps, while Ravindra Jadeja picked up three. Jadeja became only the fourth player in Test cricket history to reach the milestone of 350 wickets and 4,000 runs. He is also the first Indian left arm bowler to achieve the haul.For Hosts, Sonal Dinusha scored his maiden Test century, while Niroshan Dickwella made 80.Earlier in the day, India were bowled out for 462 in their first innings after adding just two runs in their yesterday’s score of 460 for nine. Devdutt Padikkal was India’s top scorer with 167, while KL Rahul made 82 and Dhruv Jurel contributed 51. For Sri Lanka, Prabath Jayasuriya claimed four wickets, Keshara Nuwantha took three, and Asitha Fernando picked up two.The second and final Test of the series will be played in Colombo from 23rd of this month.

. Minister of State for Petroleum and Natural Gas Suresh Gopi has informed that no decision has been taken by the Government to increase ethanol blending with petrol beyond 20 percent. In a written reply to a question in the Rajya Sabha, Mr Gopi said that any future decision regarding higher ethanol blends will be taken only after detailed scientific and technical studies and consultations with all relevant stakeholders, including automobile manufacturers and Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs).The Minister said that the Ethanol Blended Petrol (EBP) Programme has been implemented through a phased, scientifically validated and consultative process involving NITI Aayog, automobile manufacturers, OMCs  and technical institutions.He said, extensive laboratory studies and field trials covering parameters such as engine durability, emissions and fuel efficiency, have confirmed that E20 is safe for use under prescribed standards. The Minister added that these studies also established that legacy vehicles do not exhibit any significant variation in performance or abnormal wear and tear due to E20. The Minister said, these extensive laboratory studies, field validation and real-world operating experience have not established any widespread adverse impact on vehicle performance due to E20 fuel.

. An earthquake of magnitude 5.9 struck Indonesia’s Flores region early this morning, with the latest tremor occurring at a depth of around 10 kilometres. The earthquake comes days after a powerful 7.7-magnitude quake struck eastern Indonesia. The country’s National Disaster Management Agency (BNPB)  today said the death toll from a series of earthquakes has risen to 54, as authorities continue to assess the extent of casualties and damage. Rescue teams are providing medical assistance to hundreds of injured people, while the Meteorology, Climatology and Geophysics Agency said aftershocks continue in the affected areas. Authorities have deployed land, sea and air transport, including 11 aircraft and helicopters, to deliver relief supplies and support evacuation operations in remote areas, including Palue Island in Sikka Regency.

. In the FIH Hockey World Cup, the Indian men’s team will take on England in their second Pool D encounter at the Wagener Hockey Stadium in Amstelveen, the Netherlands, this evening. The match is scheduled to begin at 6:30 PM Indian Standard Time. Both teams will be looking to build on their winning starts to the tournament. India began their campaign with a 3-1 victory over Wales on Saturday, while England also made a strong start, defeating Pakistan 4-1 on the opening day.

. The government has approved 31 more applications under Electronics Components Manufacturing Scheme (ECMS) with projected investment of nearly 7,900 crore rupees. These approvals will result in a total production of electronics components worth 82 thousand crore rupees and are expected to generate over 9,500 employment opportunities. These applications have come from ten States including seven from Tamil Nadu and six each from Maharashtra and Haryana. Union Minister of Electronics and Information Technology Ashwini Vaishnaw handed over the approvals to the applicants at a function in New Delhi. The applications are related to the manufacturing of products including Acetylene Black, Speakers and microphones, Optical Transceivers, capacitors and coils. Speaking on the occasion, Mr Ashwini Vaishnaw said that with this 31 approvals, a total 106 Applications of companies have got approvals under the scheme. He informed that the government had set a target of attracting investment of 59 thousand crore rupees but now the target has crossed and achieved 69 thousand crore rupees.

. Union Home Minister Amit Shah has informed  that the government under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi destroyed the ISI-backed terror group Shahzad Bhatti Network ahead of Independence Day. He informed that the government also thwarted its plans for subversive attacks by arresting more than 200 operatives. In a social media post, he said that security forces ripped apart the network by launching coordinated operations across different locations in 14 states, upholding a brilliant example of India’s zero-tolerance towards terrorism.Our correspondent reports that the security agencies launched a coordinated multi-state operation on 12th of this month using a real-time intelligence-sharing system with State Police forces to counter Shahzad Bhatti Network -linked disruptions, planned around Independence Day. The operation led to the detention of over 200  people  across 14 states including 62  from  Uttar Pradesh, 52 from Haryana , 51 from Delhi and 44 from Punjab. Substantial recoveries, including IEDs, grenades bearing Pakistan Ordnance Factory markings, pistols, live cartridges, and CCTV cameras used for espionage, were made from the ISI-funded group.The network was involved in several terrorist activities. Shahzad Bhatti Network , a Pakistan-based, ISI-backed terror syndicate linked to grenade, IED and petrol bomb attacks and targeted killings across India. SBN has also been paying local conduits to recce police, defence and religious sites, and to install CCTV cameras for espionage. More than 80 FIRs and over 200 arrests linked to this Network have been made so far.

. US President Donald Trump today warned Oman against getting involved in a deal with Iran over control of the Strait of Hormuz, threatening to bomb it if Muscat interferes with Washington’s position on the strategic waterway. Talking to a reporter over the phone, President Trump discussed the West Asia situation as the 60-day memorandum of understanding signed with Iran in June in order to open negotiations to end the war in West Asia is set to expire. Trump said, he is not in a hurry and has not set a deadline for Iran to surrender. Asked about parallel talks between Iran and Oman over control of the Strait of Hormuz, Mr Trump said, If Oman gets in the way, the US will bomb it.The US President further indicated that the US naval blockade was continuing to put new economic pressure on the Iranian regime despite counter statements made publicly by Tehran.

. Global crude oil prices rose today. Brent crude was trading 0.4 per cent up at 88 US dollars and 90 cents per barrel in intra-day trade. West Texas Intermediate crude was trading 0.1 per cent up at 82 US dollars and 50 cents per barrel, when reports last came in.

. Ahead of Independence Day, a platform for creative expression has been provided to the youth in Uttar Pradesh. For this, the ‘Rang De Basanti’ campaign was launched. Under this campaign, the graffiti wall programme organised near Lucknow University today. Artists from the city painted public murals on the theme of a mafia-free and changing Uttar Pradesh. Through these paintings, the Uttar Pradesh of before 2017 and the changes that have taken place in Uttar Pradesh thereafter were portrayed.On the wall, artists used their colours and imagination to portray in paintings the changed positive environment in the state in terms of law and order, infrastructure and opportunities for youth. Young painter Manish Saroj’s painting expressed the pain of Uttar Pradesh suffering under mafia rule before 2017, while also presenting a positive picture of the change taking place now.Under the campaign, a comic distribution and dialogue programme will be organised in Muzaffarnagar tomorrow. During this, an original comic based on communal harmony will be distributed. Along with this, dialogues will also be held with youth in schools. On August 14, the song ‘Azadi from Fear’ of the ‘Rang De Basanti’ campaign will be launched. It will also feature a confluence of rap, music and digital art.

. Minister of State for Information and Broadcasting Dr L Murugan today said Government has established a Fact Check Unit in Press Information Bureau to mitigate fake news related to its programmes and policies. In a written reply in Lok Sabha, DR Murugan informed that the Fact Check Unit verifies claims relating to Government Ministries, Departments, PSUs and other Central Government organisations through a structured fact-checking process. It disseminates verified information through various platforms.The MoS further stated that Doordarshan and Akashvani further disseminate verified information through their news bulletins, programmes and digital platforms. DD News follows a multi-layered editorial mechanism involving rigorous fact-checking, cross-verification through multiple credible sources and editorial scrutiny before broadcast. PIB Fact Check content is regularly integrated into Doordarshan and Akashvani news and digital platforms to counter misinformation and false narratives.PIB, as the principal information dissemination agency of the Government, facilitates timely, credible and accurate communication in different forms through various media platforms. Prasar Bharati plays a key role in fulfilling the mandate of public service broadcasting. Information is disseminated in multiple languages, including regional languages and dialects, using various platforms.

. Secretary (Economic Relations) in the Ministry of External Affairs, Sudhakar Dalela, today said that during its BRICS chairship, India has placed people at the centre of collective efforts, guided by a people-centric and humanity-first approach to BRICS collaboration. He made the remarks while addressing the BRICS Civil Forum 2026 in New Delhi.He highlighted that under the chairship, over three hundred fifty meetings have been concluded across the cities, generating substantive outcomes across various sectors. He added that these engagements have strengthened the cooperation between all three foundation pillars of BRICS; which are political and security cooperation, financial collaboration and people to people partnership.Mr Dalela emphasised that BRICS reflects the growing economic weight and collective voice of emerging economies. He further said that India views BRICS as a constructive platform for dialogue and development, complementing the order and multilateral system. Talking about the Civil Forum 2026, Mr Dalela said that the inputs emerging from this event will be valuable for the BRICS Leaders Summit scheduled to be held this year.

. Indian Army Chief General Dhiraj Seth has been conferred the rank of Honorary General of the Nepal Army by President Ramchandra Paudel during an investiture ceremony at Sheetal Niwas in Kathmandu yesterday.Nepal Vice President Ram Sahaya Prasad Yadav, Foreign Minister Shisir Khanal, India’s Ambassador to Nepal Naveen Srivastava and high officials of the Nepal Army and the Nepal government were present during the ceremony. General Seth reached the Himalayan Nation on Sunday on an official visit at the invitation of his Nepalese Army counterpart, General Ashok Raj Sigdel.The conferral of the honorary rank continues a long tradition that started in 1950, under which Nepal and India confer the honorary rank of general on each other’s army chiefs.General Seth also met General Sigdel at the Nepal Army headquarters and the two leaders discussed matters of mutual interest and ways to strengthen bilateral military relations. General Seth also met Ambassador Srivastava at the Indian Embassy and the two discussed ways to further strengthen comprehensive relations between New Delhi and Kathmandu.General Seth also handed over some military and medical equipment to the Nepal Army. He planted a sapling in the premises of the Nepal Army Headquarters and received and inspected the guard of honour.

. In Chess, World No. 1 Magnus Carlsen has won Esports World Cup title for the second year in a row, by defeating Belarusian Grandmaster Denis Lazavik 2-0 in Paris, France. Representing Team Liquid, the 35-year-old Norwegian remained completely undefeated throughout the entire tournament.Meanwhile, American Grandmaster Hikaru Nakamura secured third place after defeating Alireza Firouzja 4-1 in a chaotic bronze-medal match that was repeatedly disrupted by technical problems and internet disconnections. The championship layout followed a best-of-three sets format, where the first two sets featured four games each, and a final two-game set was reserved as a tiebreaker if needed.

. Iran today said it has reached an agreement with Oman on a plan to manage the transit of ships through the Strait of Hormuz and the two sides are now working to finalize details for a joint statement. Talking to reporters in Tehran, Iranian Foreign Affairs spokesperson Esmail Baghaei said, an understanding has been reached regarding the map of the transit route.Fully reopening the waterway to commercial shipping has been a key demand of the United States, but it remains unclear whether the deal will meet Washington’s criteria. The announcement came as the 60-day negotiating period to find a peace deal between the US and Iran was expiring, with no word of an extension and both sides seemingly as far apart as they were two months ago.Iran effectively closed the strait, through which roughly one-fifth of the world’s traded oil supplies passed before the war, after Israel and the US attacked the country on 28th of February.Mideast negotiator Jared Kushner, US President Donald Trump’s son-in-law, was holding meetings with Israel’s Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, the day after he had talks with Palestinian armed group Hamas chief Khalil al-Hayya in Egypt on disarmament. The meetings with Prime Minister Netanyahu come after the Israeli leader rejected a 15-point, US-backed road map to move the truce deal forward in Gaza. Hamas said it has agreed to the road map, which includes disarmament, and the group is urging mediators and the US-created Board of Peace to compel Israel to sign on as well.But Israel, which under the road map must withdraw from Gaza, said Hamas must fully disarm before any Israeli withdrawal will occur. Israeli troops occupy about 60 per cent of the strip and Prime Minister Netanyahu has previously threatened to advance further.

. Union Minister Dr Jitendra Singh today informed that around 440 space technology startups are registered in India. In a written reply in Lok Sabha, Dr Singh said Indian National Space Promotion and Authorisation Centre, IN-SPACe has granted 113 authorisations to 52 Non-Government Entities, NGEs to carry out various space activities. Out of these, 18 NGEs are start-ups. The Minister said the Government has undertaken several proactive measures following the liberalization of the space sector. This is being done to promote participation of startups in satellite manufacturing, launch services, downstream applications and space-based technologies. IN-SPACe is facilitating the transfer of available ISRO technologies to industry while also identifying and consolidating the technology requirements of industry for future technology development and transfer. Till date, 118 Technology Transfer Agreements have been executed.

. The Qatar-India remittance service based on PosTransfer powered by UPI is now available. It enables customers in Qatar to send funds directly to UPI-enabled bank accounts in India through Qatar Post outlets. The Communications Ministry said that the service offers an instant, secure, convenient and accessible channel for cross-border remittances, particularly benefiting the large Indian community in Qatar and their families in India. The initiative combines the extensive reach of postal networks with India’s digital public infrastructure to provide an efficient and convenient channel for cross-border remittances.The Ministry informed that the service has been developed through the collaboration of Qatar Post, India Post, the Universal Postal Union’s Interconnection Platform (UPU-IP), and NPCI International Payments Limited (NIPL). It further said that India Post is also working with postal operators in other countries to operationalise additional PosTransfer powered by UPI corridors, further strengthening international financial connectivity for the Indian diaspora.
. In the forex market today, the rupee depreciated by 18 paise  to end at 95.61 rupees against the US dollar.

. The Reserve Bank of India today announced an overnight Variable Rate Reverse Repo (VRRR) auction of up to Rs 1.5 lakh crore for Tuesday, August 18, amid its review of prevailing and evolving liquidity conditions.According to a release issued today the auction will be conducted between 9.30 am and 10 am, with the funds scheduled for reversal on August 19.The announcement came after the RBI conducted two VRRR auctions on Monday. In the overnight auction, the central bank accepted Rs 96,914 crore against the notified amount of Rs 1 lakh crore, at a cut-off rate of 5.24 per cent.In a separate seven-day VRRR auction, the RBI accepted Rs 98,945 crore against the notified Rs 2 lakh crore, also at a cut-off rate of 5.24 per cent.The RBI had earlier announced the second overnight VRRR auction for Monday for Rs 1 lakh crore, with reversal scheduled for August 18.

. Youth Affairs and Sports Minister Dr Mansukh Mandaviya today interacted with MY Bharat-NSS volunteers during the Independence Day celebrations in New Delhi. Addressing the volunteers, Dr Mandaviya appreciated their contribution towards social service and encouraged them to actively participate in initiatives aimed at building a Viksit Bharat. He emphasised that the energy, commitment and innovative ideas of young people are essential for achieving the vision of a developed and self-reliant India.The Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports said that the programme also provided a platform for volunteers to share their experiences, ideas and aspirations. The interaction reaffirmed the commitment of the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports to provide meaningful opportunities for youth participation and leadership in nation-building. Around 500 students participated in the event, showcasing patriotism, national unity and collective participation.

. Union Culture Minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat today said that saree is not merely a piece of attire, rather a magnificent symbol of Indian culture. The Minister said this in a video message during Saree Shastra in New Delhi. Mr Shekhawat underlined the mastery of wearing one saree in multiple ways, the craft of designing and weaving a single saree in diverse styles. Highlighting the tradition of representing culture through sarees, he said that exhibitions and events like this help spread awareness about India’s tradition of wearing and weaving sarees, and understanding which saree suits which occasion far and wide.Minister of State for Youth Affairs and Sports Raksha Khadse said that the exhibition serves as a prime example of presenting diverse states and culture through sarees. The Minister said that the exhibition brings together artists from across the country and aims to present their work through the medium of the saree. He said, it reflects the country’s rich culture, which is being conveyed through saree craftsmanship.Saree Shastra is a three-day exhibition to honour the women who weave, preserve and wear sarees. The event reimangines the saree as one of India’s most enduring cultural artefact.

. India will host the first Global South Film Festival next year. It was announced today at a press conference held on the sidelines of the BRICS WAVES Bazaar in Mumbai. Several agreements aimed at strengthening international cooperation in the film and entertainment sector were also announced.Organisations including the National Film Development Corporation (NFDC) and the National Film Archive of India (NFAI) signed agreements, exchanged Letters of Intent and held talks with partner institutions from countries including Brazil, Russia and Vietnam. The participating organisations also agreed to explore opportunities for film co-production.The two-day WAVES BRICS Bazaar, which opened in Mumbai yesterday, concludes this evening. Prakash Magdum, Managing Director of the NFDC, said the initiative brought together more than 900 delegates from the 20 BRICS member and partner countries. Around 250 meetings were held during the one-and-a-half-day event, providing a platform for government agencies, entertainment industry professionals, investors and content creators to exchange ideas and explore opportunities for collaboration.

. India’s ace shuttler P V Sindhu has advanced to the second round of the women’s singles event at the BWF World Championships in New Delhi. The former world champion dominated Ireland’s Sophia Noble, winning 21-7, 21-11.Meanwhile, in the women’s doubles, India’s Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand have also progressed to the second round. The Indian duo defeated Spain’s Paula Lopez and Lucia Rodriguez 21-9, 21-13.

. In the FIH Women’s Hockey World Cup, India began their campaign with a thrilling 2-2 draw against China in a group-stage match at Amstelveen in the Netherlands, today.Navneet gave India an early lead in the eighth minute, but China equalised through Zhang Ying’s penalty stroke in the 15th minute. Deepika restored India’s lead in the 25th minute with a penalty-corner goal. China fought back in the third quarter, with Ma Ning converting a penalty corner in the 39th minute to level the score at 2-2. India and China are in Pool D alongside England and South Africa. The top two teams from the pool will advance to the next round.

. In the BWF Badminton World Championships, the Indian pair of M R Arjun and Hariharan Amsakarunan advanced to the second round of the men’s doubles category in New Delhi. The duo were leading 6-4 in the second game, when their opponents Scott Guildea and Paul Reynolds of Ireland retired hurt. Earlier, Arjun and Amsakarunan had won the 1st game 21-16.The Indian duo have expressed happiness after winning against their Irish opponents. Talking to the media after the match, they said the support and cheers from the home crowd helped them boost their confidence. They also noted that winning the early points in the first game helped them gain control of the match.Later in the day, former World champion and ninth seed P V Sindhu will be up against Sophia Noble of Ireland in the Women’s singles. Meanwhile, the women’s doubles duo of Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand will face Paula Lopez and Lucia Rodriguez of Spain in the first round. In the evening, Indian debutant Ayush Shetty will face World number one and defending champion Shi Yu Qi of China, in the Men’s Singles category.

. Lok Sabha has passed the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026. When the House met at 3:00 PM after the second adjournment, Union Coal and Mines Minister G Kishan Reddy moved the Bill to further amend the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act, 1957. The bill aims to make India’s mining sector more efficient, investment-friendly and well-equipped to fulfil the country’s growing demand for critical minerals. The Bill was passed without discussion amid opposition uproar.

. Over 200 Indian peacekeepers deployed with the UN mission in South Sudan have been awarded the prestigious UN medal for their exceptional service. The UN Mission in Sudan, UNMISS, in a social media post today informed that 210 Indian peacekeepers, including 6 women and 7 Staff Officers, were awarded the UN Medal for their exceptional service in Juba, South Sudan. The Mission called it a proud moment for India’s Blue Helmets. It added that through crises, medical emergencies and lifesaving missions, the courage and compassion of the Indian peacekeepers continue to protect lives and advance peace.India is the second-largest contributor of uniformed personnel to UN Peacekeeping. It currently contributes more than 4,200 military and police personnel, including 155 women to UN peace operations in various countries. These include Abyei, the Central African Republic, Cyprus, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Lebanon, the Middle East, Somalia, South Sudan and Western Sahara. As of April this year, India was the top troop contributor to UNMISS, with 1,775 Indian military personnel deployed with the UN mission.

. The Indian Army contingent has departed for Thailand today to participate in the 15th edition of the India-Thailand Joint Military Exercise MAITREE-XV (2026). The exercise, commencing tomorrow, will conclude on the 31st of this month.The  Defence Ministry said that the aim of Exercise MAITREE is to foster Military Cooperation between India and Thailand. The Exercise will enhance combined capabilities in executing Joint Counter Insurgency/ Terrorist Operations in Jungle and semi-urban environments under Chapter 7 of United Nations Charter. The training will include field exercises, combat discussions, lectures, demonstrations and a culminating validation exercise. The contingents will also exchange operational experience and showcase contemporary equipment and technologies employed during joint operations.The Ministry also said that the Indian Army and Royal Thai Army contingents comprise 85 personnel each. The Indian Army contingent is represented primarily by troops from 9 Gorkha Rifles, while the Royal Thai Army contingent comprises personnel from the 3rd Battalion, 25th Infantry Brigade, 5th Division. The exercise will involve company-level joint training focused on operations in jungle and semi-urban terrain. The Last edition of the same exercise was conducted at Foreign Training Node, Umroi, Meghalaya in September last year.

. Special initiatives will be undertaken under the Skill India Programme PM-SETU to promote Bengal’s traditional folk industries, including handloom and Dokra craft. Union Minister of State for Skill Development and Entrepreneurship,  independent charge, Jayant Chaudhary said this at a programme in Kolkata today. He said traditional industrial hubs in the state would be given priority in developing a skilled workforce in line with industry requirements.Replying to questions from journalists at the end of the ‘Kaushal Manthan’ regional conference in Kolkata, he said West Bengal had joined the PM-SETU project only two months ago, but the state would not lag behind. He said ITIs would be developed in such a way that students could be trained using the same equipment and machinery used in industries, thereby building confidence among major industrial groups in these institutions. The initiative would particularly focus on Bengal’s traditional industrial hubs.

. India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a red colour warning for very heavy rainfall to extremely heavy rainfall over Jharkhand for tomorrow. The Weather Agency forecast heavy to very heavy rainfall over Bihar, Chhattisgarh, East Madhya Pradesh, Himachal Pradesh, Odisha and West Uttar Pradesh tomorrow. According to IMD, Jammu and Kashmir, Ladakh, Uttarakhand, Punjab, Chandigarh, Haryana, Delhi, East Uttar Pradesh, West Bengal, Sikkim, North Eastern States, Karaikal, Puducherry, Tamil Nadu, Kerala and Mahe will experience heavy rainfall till Thursday. The Met Department also predicted thunderstorms accompanied with lightning and gusty winds over Gujarat, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Karnataka and Andaman and Nicobar Islands for next two to three days.IMD has advised fishermen to not venture into Arabian Sea and Bay of Bengal till tomorrow.

. In Jharkhand, following a 24-day protest by JPSC and JSSC aspirants, the state government has cancelled the 2024 JSSC-CGL examination and all competitive examinations conducted by the TDPL agency. Chief Minister Hemant Soren announced the decision yesterday evening after chairing a special Cabinet meeting.The state government has also ordered a comprehensive probe into recruitment examinations conducted by the Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC) and the Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission (JSSC) since 2014.However, student leader Piyush Kumar stated that the decision was only the first step. He added that the protesters’ demands regarding the 11th to 13th JPSC examinations and a CBI probe are still pending. The protesting students announced they would discuss their remaining demands and decide their next course of action.

. Benchmark domestic equity indices ended in the negative zone today. The Sensex dropped 281 points or 0.36 per cent to close at 77,728. The Nifty also lost 78 points or 0.32 per cent to settle at 24,288. However, the broader market at the National Stock Exchange managed to end in positive territory. The Midcap 100 index eked out a marginal gain, while the Smallcap 100 index increased 0.4 per cent.Earlier, the markets opened on a weak footing amid geopolitical uncertainty, with both benchmark indices remaining under pressure after the opening bell. However, during the afternoon session, the indices pared some of their earlier losses, though they continued to trade in negative territory.In the Sensex pack, 23 out of 30 companies registered losses. Among the top laggards, Infosys shed 2.7 per cent, HCL Tech dropped two and a half per cent and SunPharma lost 2.2 per cent. In contrast, Tata Steel advanced one and a half per cent, Axis Bank climbed one per cent and Reliance added 0.8 per cent.In the sectoral indices on the BSE, 15 out of 28 sectors ended with losses. Among the top underperformers, Information Technology declined 1.7 per cent, Focused IT dropped 1.6 per cent and Telecommunication fell by 1.2 per cent. In contrast, Realty increased 1.4 per cent, Metal gained one per cent and Capital Goods added 0.8 per cent.The overall market breadth at the BSE was negative, as shares of 2353 companies declined, 2087 advanced and 234 remained unchanged..

. The Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare has informed that the progress of area coverage under Kharif Crops has recorded more than 1000 lakh hectare area as of 14th of this month. It added that the rice has been grown over more than 379 lakh hectare area, while Oilseeds was sown over more than 184 lakh hectare area. According to the Ministry, Shri Anna cum Coarse cereals were cultivated in over 172 lakh hectare area. It added that more than 107 lakh hectare area was covered with Cotton. Additionally, the area cultivated with Pulses was recorded with area coverage of more than 108 lakh hectares. The Ministry informed that Sugarcane was grown on more than 58 lakh hectare areas, while Jute and Mesta cover more than 6 lakh hectare areas.

. In Basketball, China defeated Qatar 118-66 in the FIBA Under-18 Asia Cup competition at the Veer Savarkar Sports Complex in Ahmedabad, Gujarat today. The Chinese team dominated from the opening quarter and maintained its control throughout the game, securing a convincing 52-point victory.Meanwhile, the match between Sri Lanka and Iran is currently underway, with Iran leading when reports last came in.Later in the day, Kazakhstan will face Japan at 4:30 PM, followed by the much-anticipated match between India and South Korea at 7:30 PM.

. The Har Ghar Tiranga campaign culminated today. The fifth year of Har Ghar Tiranga  brought the Tiranga closer to millions of Indians, with people across the country coming together to hoist the National Flag, join Tiranga Yatras and sing Vande Mataram. The campaign celebrated nationwide, fostered a sense of patriotism among citizens, strengthened national unity, and promoted India’s cultural heritage. The campaign which began in 2022, has since evolved into one of the country’s largest public participation movements.This year’s campaign was dedicated to 150 years of India’s National Song, Vande Mataram, bringing together the National Flag and the National Song in a unique celebration of patriotism. One of the highlight of this year’s celebrations was the sheer variety of ways in which people participated. Across states and union territories, the spirit of Har Ghar Tiranga was visible in Tiranga Yatras, cycle and motorcycle rallies, cultural processions, school and college programmes, and community celebrations. Schools and colleges encouraged young people to learn about the National Flag and Vande Mataram. Over the past five years, Har Ghar Tiranga has grown into a nationwide expression of participation and pride. Every year  brought new ways for people to connect with the Tiranga, and 2026 has seen this participation reach an especially broad and vibrant scale.

. Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs) have remained net buyers of Indian equities during the first two week of August. According to the latest depository data, FPIs have invested 16,621 crore rupees in the domestic stock market so far this month.Of the total investment, 11,199 crore rupees came through purchases on the stock exchanges, while 5 thousand 422 crore rupees was invested through the primary market. The buying momentum, which gathered pace in July, has continued into August, supported by resilient domestic fundamentals and strong quarterly earnings.Meanwhile, buying interest was also seen in the debt market. So far in August, Foreign Portfolio Investors have invested 69 crore rupees in debt securities through the General Limit route. Through the Fully Accessible Route, FPIs have invested 972 crore rupees during the period under review.

. Sri Lanka has emerged as the country with the most positive perception of India, according to a new global survey by the Washington-based Pew Research Center. The survey, conducted between February and May this year across 36 countries and involving more than forty two thousand people, found that India continues to enjoy a largely favourable image worldwide, particularly across Europe, Asia and Africa.Sri Lanka recorded the highest rating, with 79 per cent of respondents expressing a favourable view of India. The result highlights strong regional, cultural and economic ties between the two countries. India’s substantial assistance to Sri Lanka during its 2022 economic crisis, including financial support and credit facilities, has also strengthened bilateral goodwill.The United Kingdom and Kenya followed with 71 per cent favourable views. Germany recorded 63 per cent, while Israel stood at 60 per cent. India also received positive ratings in Italy, Sweden, Japan and Thailand, each recording more than half of respondents expressing favourable views. The findings underline India’s growing global standing and the strength of its relationships with countries across Asia, Europe and Africa.

. In Football, Sporting Club Delhi defeated debutants Football Club Raengdai 5-1 in the first quarter-final of the 135th Indian Oil Durand Cup at the Birsa Munda Football Stadium in Ranchi yesterday. The victory sends Sporting Club Delhi into the semi-finals, while Football Club Raengdai’s impressive debut campaign comes to an end at the quarter-final stage.Sporting Club Delhi will face the winner of the second quarter-final between the Indian Army Football Team and East Bengal Football Club in the semi-final on Wednesday at the Vivekananda Yuba Bharati Krirangan in Kolkata.

. Union Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal held a meeting with the CEO of Check Point Software, Nadav Zafrir, in New Delhi yesterday. In a social media post, Mr Goyal said that during the meeting, they discussed the company’s growing engagement in India, including its research and development expansion and the use of AI-driven security to protect India’s digital public infrastructure.They also explored advancing cooperation in cybersecurity, digital trust, and AI-led innovation to build a resilient digital ecosystem supporting India’s technology-driven growth.The Union Minister also met the MD and CEO of Nippon Life India Asset Management Limited, Sundeep Sikka. They discussed opportunities to scale up and deepen retail investment, strengthen the asset management ecosystem, and expand avenues for attracting greater global capital into Indian markets.

. On World Elephant Day, Minister of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Bhupender Yadav, today said that Project Elephant reflects India’s commitment to protecting elephants, conserving their habitats and promoting harmonious coexistence between elephants and communities. In a social media post, Mr Yadav said that under Project Elephant, various measures are being implemented, including early warning systems and AI-based alerts to keep communities informed, solar-powered fences and trenches to protect people and elephants, and timely compensation for crop losses suffered by farmers. He added that the railways are also adopting warning signals, AI-based solutions and speed restrictions in critical corridors to prevent elephant deaths. The Minister also said that the government is promoting education and awareness to encourage communities to live in harmony with elephants.

. US President Donald Trump has instructed the Pentagon chief, Pete Hegseth, to majorly cut down upcoming joint military drills with South Korea, stating that the exercises are too expensive and send a hostile, inappropriate message to North Korea.In a social media post yesterday,  Trump explained that it was too late to completely cancel the 11-day “Ulchi Freedom Shield” exercise, which begins today. Despite Trump’s directive, South Korea’s defence ministry confirmed that the regular summer drills will proceed as planned with 18,000 South Korean troops participating. The training, which North Korea routinely denounces as a rehearsal for war, focuses heavily on modern security threats like fighting drones, stopping cyberattacks, and handling GPS disruption.

. Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) Chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey has reiterated that the new Closing Auction Session (CAS), introduced from August 3 will be continued. Speaking on the sidelines of the launch of cyber reporting platforms at the National Institute of Securities Markets (NISM), Mr. Pandey said the regulator would consider suggestions from the industry and make changes wherever necessary.The Closing Auction Session (CAS) is a 20-minute daily auction (3:15 PM to 3:35 PM) introduced by SEBI on August 3, 2026. It determines the official closing price for F&O-enabled stocks by collecting orders and matching them at a single equilibrium price. The session replaces the old Volume Weighted Average Price (VWAP) method to improve price discovery and curb late-day price manipulation.The Sebi chief added that there are no concerns around tracking error and that several participants in the industry have welcomed the move. He added some participants are yet to update their own systems, which have been built on the historical system and the VWAP system. He further noted that SEBI will soon come up with a consultation paper on the securities lending and borrowing mechanism, in its efforts to stabilise CAS.

. In Men’s Cricket, India were 288 for 2 in their first innings at stumps on day one of the first Test against hosts Srilanka at Galle International Cricket Stadium. Earlier, India won the toss and opted to bat first.Devdutt Padikkal remained unbeaten on 131 while Rishabh Pant was on 27 when stumps were drawn this evening. KL Rahul retired hurt on 77. Today’s game was cut short to 73 overs due to two rain breaks.

. Ukraine and Russia exchanged missiles and drones today, with attacks killing at least 11 people on both sides.Ukraine launched hundreds of drones across Russia in one of Kyiv’s largest aerial attacks of the war, killing six people.Five people were killed in Russia’s southwestern Rostov region after drone attacks targeted three towns. The strikes, involving more than 150 drones, also damaged several homes and a railway station and sparked a forest fire. An 83-year-old man was killed after a Ukrainian drone struck a private home in the Moscow region. Moscow’s Governor also confirmed that a Ukrainian attack triggered a fire at a Wildberries warehouse in Podolsk. Russia’s Defence Ministry said it had destroyed 822 Ukrainian drones overnight.Meanwhile, Russian strikes killed five people in Ukraine. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said a missile attack on Kryvyi Rih killed two people and injured 14 others. Further strikes killed one person in Sumy and two in Zaporizhzhia. Russia’s Defence Ministry said it had targeted a metallurgical plant in Kryvyi Rih and several military-industrial facilities in Kyiv.

. The Technology Development Board today signed an agreement with a private medical device company from Visakhapatnam for commercialisation of indigenous AI-Powered cervical cancer screening technology. The agreement will support the manufacturing and commercialization of GrivaVision, an indigenously developed, portable digital colposcope with AI-assisted capabilities for early detection of cervical pre-cancerous lesions. Through the Board’s support, the company will establish manufacturing capabilities at Kollam, Kerala, enabling commercial-scale production and wider deployment of the technology. The initiative seeks to make cervical cancer screening more accessible and affordable, particularly across primary and community healthcare settings. GrivaVision integrates a high-definition camera, an in-built display, user-friendly interface that assists gynaecologists in identifying pre-cancerous abnormalities during routine clinical examinations.

. India today launched its first-ever Guide to Grasslands and Other Open Natural Ecosystems of India at the 17th Session of the UNCCD COP17 in Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia. The document highlights the rich diversity, ecological significance and socio-economic importance of India’s grasslands, savannas, deserts and other open natural ecosystems. Speaking virtually on the sideline of the event, Union Environment, Forest and Climate Change Bhupender Yadav said that the Guide is an important step towards recognising India’s open natural ecosystems and stressed the need for their science-based conservation alongside forests. The Minister said modern science reinforces the understanding of local communities that healthy grasslands are indispensable for biodiversity, livelihoods and climate resilience.The Ministry said that the Guide brings together information on major Open Natural Ecosystems across India, covering their geographical settings, ecological characteristics, biodiversity, and the communities and tribes associated with them. It is expected to serve as a valuable resource for policymakers, researchers, conservation practitioners, development agencies and communities working towards the conservation, restoration and sustainable management of India’s grasslands and other Open Natural Ecosystems.

. The Report of the Inquiry Committee investigating allegations concerning former Allahabad High Court Judge Yashwant Varma was tabled in both the Houses of Parliament. In the Lok Sabha, Secretary General Uttpal Kuma Singh tabled the Hindi and English versions of the Report of the Inquiry Committee constituted under the Judges (Inquiry) Act, 1968 as well as the Oral and documentary evidence recorded during the course of the inquiry. While in the Rajya Sabha, the report in this regard was tabled by Secretary General P C Mody.The Judges Inquiry Committee, investigating allegations concerning Yashwant Varma, had submitted its report to the Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla in May this year. The Committee was constituted by Mr Birla on 12th of August last year to probe the allegations levelled against Justice Varma, after a sum of burnt cash was found at his official residence in New Delhi.

. The Enumeration Phase of the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of the electoral roll in Delhi concluded today. According to Office of Chief Electoral Officer of Delhi, about one crore 45 lakh forms were distributed as part of the exercise in Delhi. As part of the exercise, over 13 thousand Booth Level Officers (BLOs) visited households to distribute pre-printed enumeration forms in duplicate to all existing electors for verification and updation of the electoral rolls. Over 97 lakh enumeration forms have been digitized as of today. Claims and objections can be filed from the 24th of this month to the 23rd of September. The final electoral roll will be published on the 27th of October. Electors can fill the enumeration form online at www.voters.eci.gov.in.

. The Supreme Court has ordered stricter bail conditions for foreign nationals accused in cases under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, amid concerns over fake sureties. Issuing a slew of directions in this regard, a bench of Justices Sanjay Karol and Augustine George Masih today said, foreign nationals released on bail must deposit their passports with the jurisdictional court adding that they cannot travel outside India without prior permission.The Apex Court said, such accused must also register with the Foreigners Regional Registration Office within one week of release. The Court directed that they must normally provide two sureties for the same amount as the bail bond. The Court said, even if the residential address of an accused and other contact information etc. within India was verified during the course of investigation, the same shall be re-verified, physically, within three days of the order granting bail. It said, that the accused must also provide an affidavit on their source of income or funds in India and details of their bank accounts, if any.The court further directed authorities to create a central database containing details of foreign accused and their sureties. It said officials involved in verifying sureties, both central and state, could face departmental inquiry if the sureties are later found to be fake.The Supreme Court was hearing an NDPS case involving foreign national Chidiebere Kingsley Nawchara, who secured bail and later went on the run.

. The country’s total exports, including merchandise and services are estimated at 80.14 billion US dollars in July this year, registering a robust 13.3 per cent year-on-year growth. According to the provisional data released by the Commerce Ministry, the export performance was led by merchandise shipments, which jumped over 19.6 per cent to 44.24 billion US dollars from a year earlier. The growth in merchandise exports was driven by petroleum products, electronic goods, engineering goods, organic and inorganic chemicals, cotton yarn and handloom products. Country’s merchandise trade deficit widened by 31.5 per cent year-on-year to 15 billion US dollars last month.Cumulatively, merchandise exports during April to July period of the current financial year are estimated at 173.78 billion US dollars, registering an increase of 17 per cent on an annual basis.
